title: obistherm: Extending Ocean Biodiversity Information System Occurrence Records With Monthly Seawater Temperature
content:
ABSTRACT

Motivation

Temperature is one of the primary drivers of marine species distributions, and shifts in temperature regimes can cause profound changes in community structure. With climate change, ocean temperatures are rising beyond historical ranges in many regions and extreme temperature events are becoming more frequent. Understanding how species and ecosystems respond to these variations has become increasingly urgent. However, accessing environmental data for analyses that match species occurrence with ocean temperature involves large data sets and computational power, posing accessibility barriers to biogeographic research. To address this, we introduce obistherm, a dataset that extends the core occurrence records from the Ocean Biodiversity Information System, the largest ocean biodiversity database, with monthly seawater temperature values from four distinct satellite-derived products representing the global ocean. We match temperature values to each species occurrence location (latitude and longitude) and, when available, to the recorded depth. Additionally, obistherm provides temperature data at both the maximum and mid-depth of the site matching a species occurrence. The dataset is offered in Parquet format, a cloud-optimized columnar storage format that allows for rapid querying of millions of records within seconds. While the format is language-agnostic, we provide exemplar code and helper functions in R, Python and Julia. This new resource will facilitate integrated analyses of marine biodiversity and temperature data that advance research on thermal sensitivity and species geographic shifts, opening up new possibilities for climate-impact research on marine ecosystems.

Main Types of Variables Contained

Seawater temperature paired with geolocated species occurrence records.

Spatial Location and Grain

Global, with resolution ranging from 1 to ~10 km at the equator.

Time Period and Grain

1982 to 2026, monthly.

Major Taxa and Level of Measurement

Marine species, measured across different scales and with distinct sampling methods.

Software Format

Parquet (column-oriented format).
